column31: In my opinion, the soundtracks melody and rhythm did not generically fit the movie snippets displayed (aside from the Metropolis one). For example, the melody expected for a movie of a young girl and a dog walking deeper inside a mountain would likely benefit from using a minor scale with a slow tempo (that would change as the suspense of the scenes grow). However, it seemed the computer-generated track would sometimes fit the changes harmonically but would fail to make proper changes in terms of rhythm.

In my opinion, some of the scenes could use some silence sometimes to increase the impact and synergy with the movement in the video. 

Like, in the first one, as the girl walks towards the object she hits, the pace could slow down to match her own pace. It tends to have a constant tempo. The moment she hits with her stick calls for a certain silence and frantic movement afterwards which was only present in the second version.

The first option changed as she hits the target, but it did not match neither the mood nor what visual movement that followed. Although it was indeed changing with the scene.

The second movie could have used an octave lower extra to be relative to the size of the bully.

On the third movie, the first moments are fine in both options. However, the panic of the man that gets into the room is only represented as an increase of pace in the second version. As the owner is walking back and fourth in an almost rhythmic manner, the lower chords almost accompany each of his steps. It would have been interesting if they matched, as it would have induced correlation between visual and auditory perception.

Overall, one could cite the film amadeus in some situations: "Too many notes". It felt like that at times, the moments called for less auditory movement and felt a bit too much all over the place. At other times, the increase of notes actually matched the movement accordingly.

column31: I really enjoyed the music. I wouldn’t say it sounded computer generated. I found all the tracks pleasant to listen to. However, the scenes presented were more adventurous or comedic.
